verdicts.reasoning: All ten stems place two single pieces of money side by side and demand a value judgement between them, and both directions are exercised — 'smaller value' at seed 11, 'greater value' at seed 64 — so the pupil cannot pass by always picking the bigger face.
verdicts.content_note_from_attester: Seeds 23, 91 and 103 draw only one of the two things being compared (seed 103 renders the ₱10 coin alone, with no ₱1 coin), so the visual cannot settle the comparison it accompanies.

verdicts.reasoning: No sample pairs a denomination with itself: seed 11 sets ₱10 against ₱5 and seed 118 sets ₱20 against ₱100, and across the set the pairs range over ₱1/₱5, ₱5/₱50, ₱10/₱50 and ₱50/₱100, so the pupil meets many distinct denomination pairings.
verdicts.content_note_from_attester: 'They are equal' appears as an option in every sample but is never the key, since no pair is ever of equal value — a consistent giveaway a test-wise pupil could exploit.

verdicts.reasoning: Peso coins are the compared objects, not scenery: seed 11 weighs a ₱10 coin against a ₱5 coin, and seeds 91 and 103 both turn on the ₱1-versus-₱10/₱5 coin pair, with the coin itself drawn in the payload.

Not a single centavo piece appears anywhere in this set — not in a stem, not in an option, not in a payload. The smallest denomination in play is the ₱1 coin, and full option lists such as seed 42's and seed 78's consist purely of peso coins, peso bills and 'They are equal'.

Bills are compared in both configurations: against a coin at seed 42 (₱5 coin vs ₱50 bill) and against another bill at seeds 118 and 127 (₱20 vs ₱100, ₱50 vs ₱100), so paper money is exercised as a full participant in the comparison.

₱100 is the largest value present and it is worked from both sides — it is the greater item at seed 23 and the thing that exceeds the keyed answer at seed 127 — while nothing above the ₱100 ceiling appears in any stem, option or payload.
